bibliography.title: Facial Contouring in Orthognathic Surgery: The Role of Facial Implants
bibliography.authors: Brito GC, de Moraes M, Faverani L, Olate S.

study.research_problem: Facial implants are used simultaneously with orthognathic surgery to refine contour, but indications, implant/material selection, design, technique, fixation, soft-tissue requirements, outcomes, and timing are not standardized.
study.exact_gap: The literature lacks an integrated map of where and why stock or patient-specific facial implants are placed during orthognathic surgery and what clinical/esthetic outcomes and complications are actually reported (S001:C01-S002:C02).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Map types, indications, surgical techniques, materials, anatomical sites, and clinical outcomes of facial implants placed concomitantly with orthognathic surgery using a PCC-framed scoping review (S003:C01-S004:C01).
study.study_design: PRISMA-ScR and OSF-registered scoping review of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and LILACS with dual screening, third-reviewer resolution, standardized charting, qualitative/descriptive synthesis, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment (S003:C01-S006:C02).
study.sample_or_model: Seventeen human reports from 1998-2025, dominated by retrospective studies, small prospective studies, case reports/series, and a technical note, covering malar, infraorbital, paranasal, chin, mandibular body, and angle augmentation (S007:C01-S009:C01).
comparators: Patient-specific versus stock implants in limited reports
Different materials and anatomical sites, mostly without concurrent controls
Simultaneous versus staged implantation discussed largely through external contextual literature
No standardized cross-study comparator or outcome set
method_spine: Define population, concept, and context rather than an efficacy PICO.
Chart anatomy, indication, implant type/material, surgical procedure, fixation, outcome, complication, and follow-up.
Separate included-study evidence from external literature used only for context.
Map technique and implementation constraints alongside outcomes.
Use qualitative evidence-mapping language because quality was not appraised and comparative data are sparse.

verification: The review reports registration, databases, a sample search strategy, dual screening, adjudication, charting variables, and PRISMA-ScR flow (S003:C01-S007:C01).

The design-count sentence appears internally inconsistent with 17 included studies: six retrospective plus two prospective plus seven case reports/series plus one technical note totals 16, so source categories should be checked against the underlying table (S007:C01).
validation: No formal quality or risk-of-bias appraisal was performed, consistent with the stated scoping purpose but limiting safety/effectiveness inference (S006:C02).
The review contains no mechanical, geometric, manufacturing, or prospective clinical validation of any implant class.
sensitivity: No subgroup, sensitivity, certainty, or publication-bias analysis is reported; follow-up and outcome definitions vary widely (S009:C01; S014:C01).
Discussion themes integrate external literature, which can aid interpretation but must not be counted as additional included evidence (S006:C02; S010:C01).
application_prediction: Patient-specific PEEK/titanium, simultaneous placement, and staged placement are presented as planning options whose comparative long-term value, cost, and soft-tissue behavior remain uncertain (S014:C02-S015:C01).

primary_outcomes: Included implants spanned PEEK, porous polyethylene, silicone, hydroxyapatite, PMMA, and titanium across multiple midface/lower-face sites; PEEK was usually patient-specific and porous polyethylene often stock (S008:C01).
Follow-up ranged roughly 0.5-6 years and outcomes were primarily qualitative, with no standardized functional, esthetic, imaging, or patient-reported outcome set (S009:C01; S014:C01).

Selected reports described low complication rates, transient symptoms, revisions, exposures, and high satisfaction, but most evidence came from uncontrolled series/cases and site/material-specific contexts (S014:C01-S014:C02).

The review emphasizes practical moderators: soft-tissue envelope, pocket design, nerve protection, muscular forces, fixation, surgeon participation in design, edema, and simultaneous-versus-staged timing (S012:C03-S014:C03).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Qualitative clinical evidence map dominated by small observational reports; useful for taxonomy and implementation hypotheses, not comparative efficacy, mechanical performance, or pooled safety.

argument_map.central_claim: Alloplastic facial implants may be useful adjuncts to orthognathic surgery, and patient-specific designs may improve anatomical planning/fit, but sparse uncontrolled evidence, heterogeneous outcomes, absent quality appraisal, and strong dependence on site, soft tissue, fixation, and surgical execution prevent comparative or long-term claims.
data: Seventeen heterogeneous human reports charted by anatomy, material/design, indication, procedure, outcomes, complications, and follow-up (S007:C01-S009:C01).
Qualitative material, technique, outcome, and implementation themes (S011:C01-S015:C01).
argument_map.warrant: Repeated clinical feasibility across sites/materials can justify an evidence map and design considerations, while treatment recommendations require quality-appraised comparative data and standardized patient-important outcomes.
backing: The review explicitly states that outcomes are qualitative and evidence is largely case reports/small series, limiting safety, effectiveness, predictability, and long-term inference (S014:C01; S015:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Potential adjunct under anatomy-, material-, fixation-, soft-tissue-, and operator-dependent conditions.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: A scoping review maps literature and does not estimate comparative treatment effects.
No formal risk-of-bias appraisal means reported favorable outcomes cannot be weighted by credibility (S006:C02).
PEEK, titanium, porous polyethylene, silicone, HA, and PMMA have different tissue interactions, fixation, imaging, and complication profiles.
Stock versus PSI and simultaneous versus staged placement are not isolated by common comparators.
Soft-tissue edema/adaptation, nerve/muscle anatomy, pocket and fixation can dominate the realized result despite geometric fit (S012:C03-S014:C03).
Statements sourced from contextual external literature must not be presented as findings of the 17-study evidence base.

measured: At review level, search/selection and charted study characteristics; all complication, satisfaction, symmetry, contour, exposure, infection, and follow-up observations originate in included clinical reports (S006:C01-S009:C01; S014:C01-S014:C02).
inferred: Improved anatomic fit, reduced displacement, surgical efficiency, infection resistance, osseointegration, and material-mechanics advantages are synthesized from limited reports and contextual sources rather than directly compared across the included evidence (S012:C01-S012:C03).
The value of staged versus simultaneous placement is inferred from edema/soft-tissue adaptation and external practice literature (S014:C02-S014:C03).
recommended: Develop standardized outcome sets, comparative cohorts/trials, longer follow-up, quality appraisal, cost/resource reporting, imaging/soft-tissue simulation validation, and anatomy/material-specific complication surveillance (S015:C01).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Anatomic fit or symmetry is not equivalent to mechanical durability, patient satisfaction, or functional benefit.
Porosity or modulus descriptions do not demonstrate in-vivo integration or lower infection risk in a given device.
Qualitative contour photographs do not provide standardized esthetic effect or soft-tissue stability.
Zero complications in a small series does not estimate population safety.
Concomitant placement feasibility does not prove it is preferable to staged placement.
overclaim_risks: Material statements such as porous titanium matching bone mechanics or a porous surface resisting infection can be mistaken for findings of this review's clinical evidence (S012:C01-S012:C02).
Calling PSI outcomes predictable, stable, or reliable exceeds the predominantly uncontrolled qualitative evidence (S014:C01-S014:C02).
The automatic porous/lattice cue reflects named implant materials, not a scaffold-engineering study; animal and in-vivo experimental cues are also incorrect for this review.

section_moves.move: Use PCC to bound an evidence-mapping question
section_moves.execution: The review fixes population, concept, and context to human orthognathic surgery with simultaneous stock or custom facial implant placement (S004:C01-S005:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Use PCC for broad device-landscape mapping and reserve PICO/effect language for questions with comparable interventions and outcomes.
section_moves.failure_mode: A broad PCC map does not support comparative efficacy.

section_moves.move: Map anatomy, material/design, intervention purpose, and evidence type together
section_moves.execution: The review cross-references facial region, material, stock/PSI status, indication, study design, and follow-up (S007:C01-S009:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For heterogeneous implant literature, organize the matrix as anatomy x indication x material/design x fixation x study design x follow-up before discussing outcomes.
section_moves.failure_mode: Material names alone are too coarse to infer performance.

section_moves.move: Add implementation anatomy to geometric-fit claims
section_moves.execution: The review details nerve protection, soft-tissue envelope, pocket, muscle sling, edema, screw fixation, exposure, and intraoperative positioning (S012:C03-S014:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A patient-specific implant Discussion should trace virtual fit through access, registration, fixation, soft tissue, dynamic forces, and postoperative adaptation.
section_moves.failure_mode: A CAD-perfect device may be surgically unplaceable or clinically malpositioned.

section_moves.move: Label contextual literature separately from included evidence
section_moves.execution: The methods state that external literature is used to contextualize themes and is not an expansion of the review evidence base (S006:C02; S010:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In scoping reviews, tag every citation as included evidence or contextual source so readers know which claims were systematically selected.
section_moves.failure_mode: Context citations can silently inflate apparent evidence coverage.

section_moves.move: End with an evidence-map conclusion and research architecture
section_moves.execution: The summary limits claims to possible adjunctive value and requests standardized outcomes, comparisons, follow-up, cost-effectiveness, and better soft-tissue simulation (S015:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A scoping review conclusion should state what categories exist, where evidence clusters, which comparisons are absent, and the minimum next-study design.
section_moves.failure_mode: Do not rank treatments when quality and comparability were not assessed.

author_reported: Substantial methodological heterogeneity, predominantly observational evidence, qualitative outcomes, nonstandard follow-up, limited comparisons, and insufficient long-term inference (S001:C01; S009:C01; S014:C01-S015:C01).
reader_identified: No risk-of-bias or quality assessment, so favorable case series cannot be weighted against stronger or weaker designs.
Included-study design counts appear inconsistent with the stated total of 17 (S007:C01).
No standardized functional, esthetic, imaging, PROM, complication, or revision outcome set.
Multiple anatomy/material/design/fixation combinations and variable follow-up prevent meaningful pooled safety or effectiveness.
External contextual citations may be confused with systematically included evidence.
No engineering validation of porosity, modulus, fit, fixation, fatigue, or integration and no cost-effectiveness data.
Likely publication and case-selection bias toward notable esthetic successes or unusual complications.
likely_bias_direction: Uncontrolled favorable case reports and surgeon-authored technical reports likely overstate predictability and understate harms.
Material/mechanism discussion may imply stronger evidence than the included clinical studies provide.
Short and irregular follow-up may miss late exposure, migration, bone resorption, infection, or revision.
limitations.scope_boundary: This scoping review maps clinical use and implementation considerations for simultaneous facial implants; it does not establish comparative material superiority, mechanical performance, pooled safety, optimal timing, or long-term effectiveness.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Use a PCC-framed anatomy x indication x material/design x fixation x evidence-type matrix for heterogeneous implant landscapes.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Scoping-review Methods, evidence map, and Results taxonomy.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A broad map without quality appraisal cannot support comparative efficacy or material ranking.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Extend patient-specific fit narratives through access, registration, fixation, nerve/muscle anatomy, soft-tissue envelope, edema, and dynamic loading.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Device Methods, translational Discussion, and failure-mode audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Virtual geometric fit can fail during surgical placement or postoperative soft-tissue adaptation.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate systematically included evidence from contextual literature and constrain conclusions when no risk-of-bias appraisal was performed.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Scoping-review citation audit, Discussion, and conclusion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: External mechanism claims cannot be counted as findings of the charted corpus.

critical_weaknesses: No quality appraisal and predominantly low-level uncontrolled evidence.
Nonstandard qualitative outcomes and heterogeneous sites/materials/designs.
Potential mixing of included and contextual evidence and inconsistent design counts.

summary_zh: 这是一篇 PRISMA-ScR 范围综述，目标是绘制正颌手术同期面部植入物的解剖部位、材料、stock/PSI、适应证、术式和结局，不是多孔支架工程实验。17 篇人类证据以回顾性研究、病例系列/报告和技术说明为主，作者明确未做风险偏倚评估，结局也多为定性，因此只能做 evidence map。其最有价值之处是提醒：患者特异性不止是 CAD 贴合，还要经过手术入路、神经/肌肉保护、实体定位、螺钉固定、软组织包膜、肿胀和动态咀嚼力。讨论还混入了用于背景解释的外部文献，Skill 会要求把这些与系统纳入证据显式标记。任何‘PEEK/钛可靠、孔隙促进整合、PSI 更优’的句子都应降到材料或临床假说，除非有质量可评的比较数据。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including methods, included-design counts, material/anatomy mapping, operative constraints, outcomes, and staged-versus-simultaneous discussion.
The porous/lattice cue reflects mentioned materials rather than a scaffold-engineering experiment; animal cues are incorrect.
The paper is a strong exemplar for scoping taxonomy and surgical-realization constraints, not for comparative efficacy.
